title: Sweat

teacherSummary.text: Delia Jones, a washerwoman in Eatonville, Florida, has supported her abusive husband Sykes for fifteen years. Sykes wants her out of the house for his mistress and terrorizes her with a rattlesnake he keeps in a box. One night the snake gets loose; Sykes, in the dark, is bitten. Delia, hearing his cries, does not help, and waits under the Chinaberry tree as he dies.

segments.activity: Independent annotation and a claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph (exemplar given).
segments.script: Annotate the story for irony, symbolism (three marks with a margin note each), then write one claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph: what does this story suggest about endurance turning to justice? Then start your writing prompt at your assigned level (HS Sophomore: Analyze how Sweat develops the idea of endurance turning to justice. Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of symbolism and characterization shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.) Exemplar: Delia's labor gives her a moral claim to the home that Sykes tries to take. When the text says “Mah tub of suds is filled yo' belly with vittles more times than yo' hands is filled it” (Sweat, paragraph 20), it shows this directly. She tells him "Mah tub of suds is filled yo' belly with vittles more times than yo' hands is filled it," and sums up fifteen years as "Sweat, sweat, sweat!"; when Sykes's own snake kills him, the story lets her keep what she earned.
